title: Domain of the special-fibre normal-cone trace
statement:
Fix the global finite-field and finite coefficient conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, an integer $n\geq1$, and $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $X,C$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $c:C\to X\times_kX$ be a geometric correspondence, and let $Z\hookrightarrow X$ be closed. Form the Rees deformation of [lem-trf-dnc-functorial-geometry] and its special-fibre correspondence
$$b=(b_1,b_2):N_{c^{-1}(Z\times Z)/C}\longrightarrow N_{Z/X}\times_kN_{Z/X}.$$
The two normal cones, their products and the fixed scheme of $b$ are separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Their legs, projections, diagonal, fixed-square maps and structure morphisms are separated of finite type, admit finite-type compactifications, and admit compactifications of finite topological dimension. Every bounded constructible finite-Tor coefficient complex on these schemes, in the ordinary constant-$A$ small pro-etale categories of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], has a bounded-below etale-origin witness. For these morphisms the relative constructible exceptional adjunction of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class], finite-Tor constructible preservation of [thm-sf-preservation-class], and finite-stage composition, compact-support and exchange assertions of [prop-functor-package] apply. In particular, let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ and $u:c_2^*K\to c_1^!K$ be an admissible cohomological correspondence as in [def-trf-correspondence]. Its specialized coefficient $M=\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde X_Z}K$ of [def-trf-deformation-specialization] is in $D^b_{ctf}(N_{Z/X},A)$, and the specialized coefficient morphism on $b$ has a Verdier trace class in the same constructible finite-coefficient framework of [def-trf-trace-class]. These assertions concern the constructible relative adjunction; they assert no unrestricted unbounded pro-etale adjoint.

proof.text: The Rees construction in [lem-trf-dnc-functorial-geometry] applies to the closed pair $Z\hookrightarrow X$ and to the inverse-image pair $c^{-1}(Z\times Z)\hookrightarrow C$. Its special fibres are the normal cones described by [pur9-def-normal-cone], and functoriality gives the lifted correspondence whose special fibre is $b=(b_1,b_2):N_{c^{-1}(Z\times Z)/C}\to N_{Z/X}\times_kN_{Z/X}$.

The normal-cone projections and the two legs of $b$ are obtained by base change and composition from separated finite-type maps in the preceding construction. The fixed scheme is the fibre product of $b$ with the relative diagonal, as in [def-trf-fixed-scheme]; products and these base changes preserve separatedness and finite type. Thus all schemes and maps named in the statement are separated and of finite type over $k$.

Every separated finite-type map in this finite-type $k$-setting has a dense finite-type compactification by [thm-nagata-compactification]. Since each source is finite type over the field $k$, [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] gives finite topological dimension for the compactification; applying these two results to the projections, legs, diagonals, fixed-square maps and structure maps gives the compactifications required in the statement.

For $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, the specialization construction of [def-trf-deformation-specialization] is available on the separated finite-type Rees lift. The specialization zero-section theorem [lem-trf-specialization-zero-section] gives $M=\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde X_Z}K\in D^b_{ctf}(N_{Z/X},A)$. By [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], every bounded constructible finite-Tor object on each resulting scheme has a bounded-below etale-origin witness in the ordinary constant-$A$ pro-etale categories.

For each separated finite-type map just listed, [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] supplies the relative constructible exceptional adjunction and [thm-sf-preservation-class] keeps bounded finite-Tor constructible inputs in the stated category. The finite-stage composition, compact-support, exchange and projection assertions are exactly the corresponding clauses of [prop-functor-package], so the specialized legs and fixed-square maps satisfy the required finite-stage functorial framework. These results are relative to the witnessed bounded-below domain and make no unrestricted unbounded pro-etale assertion.

The specialized morphism on $b$ is therefore a morphism of the same admissible constructible coefficient type as in [def-trf-correspondence]. Applying the trace-class construction [def-trf-trace-class] to $b$, with its fixed scheme from [def-trf-fixed-scheme] and coefficient $M$, produces the Verdier trace class. This proves the final assertion while retaining the finite-coefficient and constructible-relative domain specified in the statement.

split_report.summary: Audited the imported omnibus domain statement against Varshavsky §§1.3–1.4 and Theorem 2.1.3(b). The proof now has six steps: Rees normal-cone geometry, finite-type fixed-square geometry, compactifications and dimension, constructible specialization and etale origin, relative adjunction/preservation and finite-stage functor package, and application of the Verdier trace-class definition. All steps cite existing DAG nodes; no new node was needed.
